reading.body:
Michigan's indexed data center facilities number six, but the dataset records zero megawatts of total capacity, which means the power dimension of this state's footprint cannot be assessed from what is published here.

The six facilities are spread across the southeastern quadrant of the state, concentrated near Detroit and Lansing. Only one, EdgeConneX Detroit DET01 in Oakland County, carries a square footage figure of 39,900 square feet. The others have no physical scale data attached. One entry, listed as a Chick-fil-A Hiring Center operated by Dennis Sampier, appears to be a geocoding or categorization error rather than a functioning data center.

For AI infrastructure purposes, the absence of megawatt figures is the critical gap. Compute capacity is bounded by available power, and power is what this dataset does not provide. Square footage for a single facility gives a partial sense of physical plant, but without load data it cannot be connected to any estimate of compute density or AI workload potential. What the data covers is location and operator identity for a small set of Michigan facilities. What it does not cover is everything needed to judge whether those facilities are relevant to AI scaling.
